title: Business Requirements Document — New Requirements Chat

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body:
The proposed Hospital Management System (HMS) aims to establish a centralized, secure, and interoperable platform for managing comprehensive hospital operations. The strategic rationale for this system is to transition from fragmented operational processes to a unified digital ecosystem that handles patient information, medical records, appointments, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory management. 

Currently, the source specification provides a high-level functional overview but lacks the technical depth and specific compliance mappings required for a production-grade healthcare system. To ensure viability in the healthcare industry, this BRD mandates strict adherence to applicable compliance frameworks, specifically HIPAA, GDPR (for EU patients), HL7 FHIR, and DICOM. The system must not only support the core operational workflows (e.g., patient registration to discharge) but also guarantee the security, privacy, and interoperability of Protected Health Information (PHI) to meet regulatory standards and operational benchmarks.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body:
**Business Objectives:**
1. **Centralized Operations:** Consolidate hospital operations (OPD/IPD, billing, pharmacy, lab) into a single platform to reduce administrative overhead and improve data consistency.
2. **Regulatory Compliance:** Achieve full compliance with HIPAA Security Rule and GDPR to ensure legal operation and protection of patient privacy.
3. **Interoperability:** Enable seamless data exchange with external healthcare providers and imaging devices using standard protocols.
4. **Operational Resilience:** Ensure high availability and rapid recovery in the event of system failures to prevent life-threatening downtime.

**Success Metrics (NFR Benchmarks):**
*   **PHI Security:** 100% of PHI encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2+ (per HIPAA §164.312).
*   **Audit Integrity:** 100% of audit logs must be immutable and tamper-proof.
*   **Disaster Recovery:** Recovery Time Objective (RTO) < 1 hour; Recovery Point Objective (RPO) < 5 minutes.
*   **Interoperability:** 100% of clinical data exchange conforming to HL7 FHIR R4 standards; imaging data conforming to DICOM.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body:
**In Scope:**
*   **Core Modules:** Authentication, Patients, Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, Laboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
*   **Workflows:** Complete patient journey (Registration → Appointment → Consultation → Diagnosis → Lab/Pharmacy → Billing → Follow-up) and inpatient journey (Admission → Bed Allocation → Treatment → Investigations → Discharge → Final Billing).
*   **User Roles:** Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient.
*   **Compliance Controls:** Implementation of RBAC, audit logging, data encryption, and backup/recovery mechanisms.

**Out of Scope (Open Items Requiring Stakeholder Input):**
*   **Specific Data Retention Policies:** The source document does not specify legal retention periods (e.g., 7-10 years) or archival strategies (e.g., S3 Glacier). This is a critical gap requiring legal and compliance stakeholder input.
*   **Threat Modeling Details:** Specific attack vectors (e.g., SQL injection, XSS) and network segmentation rules are not defined in the source and require a dedicated security architecture phase.
*   **Hardware Integration Specifics:** While DICOM is required for interoperability, specific hardware device integrations are not detailed in the source.

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body:
**System Users (Personas):**
*   **Admin:** Full system configuration, user management, and oversight.
*   **Doctor:** Clinical dashboards, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes.
*   **Nurse:** Nursing notes, vital signs, and patient care tasks.
*   **Receptionist:** Patient registration, appointment scheduling, and queue management.
*   **Pharmacist:** Pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory management.
*   **Lab Technician:** Laboratory test requests and report generation.
*   **Accountant:** Billing, payments, insurance management, and hospital expenses.
*   **Patient:** Portal access to view appointments, prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history.

**Governance & Compliance Stakeholders (Implied by Domain Profile):**
*   **HIPAA Compliance Officer:** Responsible for verifying Administrative, Physical, and Technical safeguards (45 CFR 164.312).
*   **Data Protection Officer (DPO):** Ensures GDPR compliance for EU patient data.
*   **IT Security Architect:** Oversees threat modeling, encryption standards (AES-256), and network security.
*   **Clinical Informatics Lead:** Ensures HL7 FHIR and DICOM standards are correctly implemented for data exchange.

sections.title: 5. Business Requirements Specification Matrix
table: System must allow registration of patients and management of their profiles, including PII and medical history.
Patient data is encrypted at rest (AES-256); PII is masked in logs; profile creation is successful via UI.
System must store and manage clinical notes, diagnosis, treatment history, allergies, and vital signs.
Clinical data is structured for HL7 FHIR R4 exchange; audit logs for EMR access are immutable.
System must enforce granular access controls for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Tech, Accountant, and Patient.
Nurse cannot access billing data; Doctor cannot modify another Doctor's notes; MFA enforced for staff.
System must manage lab test requests and generate reports, supporting interoperability with external labs.
Lab results are exchanged via HL7 FHIR Observation resources; DICOM support for imaging if applicable.
System must handle billing, payments, insurance management, invoices, and receipts.
Payment data is PCI-DSS compliant; PHI is not stored in payment logs; accurate invoice generation.
System must maintain comprehensive, tamper-proof audit logs for all user actions and data access.
Audit logs are written to append-only storage; access restricted to security admins; logs meet HIPAA/GDPR accountability.
System must ensure high availability and rapid recovery from failures.
RTO < 1 hour; RPO < 5 minutes; active-active or active-passive replication verified.
System must support HL7 FHIR for clinical data and DICOM for medical imaging.
API endpoints conform to FHIR resources (Patient, Encounter, Observation); DICOM conformance statements defined.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body:
**Assumptions:**
1. The system will be deployed in a cloud or on-premise environment as per the source document, but specific infrastructure details are pending.
2. The suggested tech stack (React/Next.js, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot, PostgreSQL/MySQL, Redis) is acceptable for the initial phase, subject to security review.
3. Users will have basic digital literacy to interact with the web-based UI and patient portal.

**Operational Constraints:**
1. **Compliance Mandate:** The system cannot go live without a verified HIPAA Security Rule Compliance Matrix and GDPR data handling protocols.
2. **Data Integrity:** Database integrity must be maintained through regular backups and transactional consistency.
3. **Performance:** API responses must be fast to support real-time clinical decision-making; specific latency benchmarks are not defined in the source and require further definition.
4. **Security:** Secure authentication (JWT/OAuth), password encryption, and session management are mandatory constraints.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body:
**Risk Factors (from Audit):**
1. **Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards (HIGH):** The source lacks AES-256/TLS 1.2+ mandates. *Mitigation:* Explicitly specify AES-256 for PHI at rest and TLS 1.2/1.3 for transit; define KMS strategy.
2. **Absence of Audit Trail Immutability (HIGH):** Audit logs are not defined as tamper-proof. *Mitigation:* Use append-only storage or blockchain-based ledger; define retention and access controls.
3. **Missing Interoperability Standards (HIGH):** No HL7 FHIR/DICOM references. *Mitigation:* Integrate FHIR R4 for clinical data and DICOM for imaging; define conformant API endpoints.
4. **Undefined Disaster Recovery Benchmarks (MEDIUM):** No RTO/RPO specified. *Mitigation:* Define RTO < 1h and RPO < 5min; specify replication strategies.
5. **Ambiguous RBAC Granularity (MEDIUM):** Role access details are unclear. *Mitigation:* Define a detailed RBAC matrix mapping roles to CRUD permissions per data entity; implement least-privilege.

**Compliance Baseline (Missing Sections):**
*   **HIPAA Security Rule Compliance Matrix (CRITICAL):** Must map technical controls to 45 CFR 164.312 (Administrative, Physical, Technical safeguards).
*   **HL7 FHIR and DICOM Integration Specification (HIGH):** Must specify FHIR R4 resource models and DICOM conformance.
*   **Data Retention and Archival Policy (HIGH):** Must define retention periods (e.g., 7-10 years) and archival workflows.
*   **Disaster Recovery and Business Continuity Plan (CRITICAL):** Must detail failover procedures and testing schedules.
*   **Threat Modeling and Security Architecture (HIGH):** Must include STRIDE threat model and OWASP Top 10 mitigations.

_source_audit.summary: The document provides a high-level functional overview of a Hospital Management System (HMS), listing core modules (EMR, Billing, Pharmacy, etc.) and a suggested tech stack (React, FastAPI/Node, PostgreSQL). However, it lacks the technical depth, specific compliance mappings (HIPAA/GDPR), data standards (HL7 FHIR/DICOM), and non-functional benchmarks required for a production-grade healthcare system. It reads as a generic software requirements outline rather than a rigorous architectural specification.

risk_factors.title: Lack of Specific PHI Encryption Standards
risk_factors.description: The document mentions 'password encryption' and 'privacy of medical information' but fails to specify encryption standards for Protected Health Information (PHI) at rest or in transit. It does not mandate AES-256 for data at rest or TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, which are HIPAA Security Rule requirements.
risk_factors.mitigation: Explicitly specify AES-256 encryption for all PHI fields in the database and TLS 1.2/1.3 for all API communications. Define key management strategies (e.g., KMS) for encryption keys.

risk_factors.title: Absence of Audit Trail Immutability

risk_factors.mitigation: Specify that audit logs must be written to an append-only storage system or blockchain-based ledger to ensure immutability. Define retention periods and access controls for audit logs.

Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
